chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Hamid, from Abu Jamilah, from Abu Usamah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding a man who is in a state of major ritual impurity (junub) and has no water with him, while he is the Imam of the people, he said: 'Yes, he performs dry ablution (tayammum) and leads them in prayer.'

And from it, what was narrated: Sa'd ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Abdillah ibn Bukayr, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who became junub, then performed tayammum, and led us in prayer while we were in a state of purity (having performed wudu/ghusl), and he said: 'There is no harm in it.'

And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Humran and Jamil ibn Darraj, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): An Imam of a people was affected by major impurity during travel, and he did not have with him enough water for ghusl. Should some of them perform wudu and pray behind him? He said: 'No, but the junub should perform tayammum and pray behind them, for indeed Allah, Exalted and Majestic, made the earth a purifier.'

And from him, from Abu Ja'far, from his father, from Abdillah ibn al-Mughirah, from Abdillah ibn Bukayr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I said to him: A man led a people in prayer while he was junub and had performed tayammum, while they were in a state of purity, and he said: 'There is no harm in it.'

The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And the missed prayer is made up with adhan and iqamah if the person missed that. We have already presented what indicates this, and what increases its clarification is what he narrated:

key_terms.طَهُورٌ: In a state of ritual purity
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no harm in it (permissible)
key_terms.يُجْنِبُ: To be in a state of major ritual impurity (junub)

ai.seo_question: Can an Imam who is junub and has no water for ghusl lead the congregation in prayer after performing tayammum?
ai.summary: These narrations from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establish the permissibility of a *junub* Imam leading congregational prayer via *tayammum* when water is scarce, emphasizing that his state of impurity does not invalidate the validity of the followers' prayers. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the Imam's ritual state is distinct from the congregation's, ensuring communal worship continues uninterrupted during travel or necessity. The inclusion of performing *adhan* and *iqamah* during makeup prayers underscores the procedural completeness required to rectify missed ritual elements.
